title: Mar Zutra son of Rav Mari
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: Kiddushin 65b relates that Mar Zutra and Rav Ada (or Acha) Saba, the sons of Rav Mari bar Isur, divided their property and came before Rav Ashi, etc.

Hyman regards this Mar Zutra as Ravina’s colleague, younger than he but discussing matters with him, as in Pesachim 62a: Mar Zutra son of Rav Mari said to Ravina, “(Rav Chisda) teaches ‘since.’” In Kiddushin 7a he said to him, “Was it not taught?”; there, 21a, he said to him, “One can refute”; in Bava Kamma 29b he said to him, “Is it comparable? This is comparable only to this”; in Bava Metzia 55a, “Rav (Hyman proposes Mar) Zutra said to him: What did you see?” etc.; there, 106a, he said to him, “If so”; in Zevachim 22a he said to him, “What is it for his son? Rather, from him, to exclude”; there, 48b, he said to him, “And is there not tithe?”; there, 50a, he said to him, “Tithe, which is merely unconsecrated”; in Menachot 56a he said to him, “According to Rabbi Yehudah too, what was included?” etc.; in Chullin 108a he said to him, “After all, according to whom did Rav speak? … Shall we say he disagrees with Rava?”; and in Temurah 19a he said to him, “So too it is reasonable.” Their disputes we find in Bava Metzia 67b and Bava Batra 7b. Seder HaDorot wrote that this Ravina is the early one; Hyman rejects this, arguing that he lived in the time of Rav Ashi and Ravina and was younger than he. Explicit proof is from Chullin 108a, where he said to Ravina, “Shall we say he disagrees with Rava?” — and the early Ravina whom they mention lived in Rav Yosef’s days.

In Chullin 49a: Rav Acha bar Natan (Dikdukei Soferim: Rav Acha bar Rav) said, “We attribute it”; Mar Zutra son of Rav Mari said, “We do not attribute it.” “Rav Shmuel son of Rabbi Abbahu said: Father was one of the heads of the kallah of Rafram, and he said, ‘We attribute it.’ They said this before Mar Zutra son of Rav Mari, and he did not accept it.” Hyman also infers from this that he lived in the time of Rav Ashi and Ravina, for Rav Shmuel lived in the time of the Savoraim. He is mentioned in Nazir 22b, where he said, “This is what Rami bar Chama [said].”
In Nedarim 4a he disagrees with Rav Acha son of Rav Ika.

notes.text: בלי דרפרם is read כלי דרפרם, the kallah of Rafram, as disclosed before. RavAcha barNatan versus barRav, and Rav-to-Mar correction, remain supplied/attributed alternatives; note the related entry’s Ada form without automatic harmonization. Hyman’s late Ravina/Savoraim argument remains his chronology, not an authority merge.

The consulted Kiddushin 65b names Mar Zutra and Rav Ada Saba as sons of Rav Mari bar Isur. Hyman’s Acha alternative remains alongside Ada, and his Rav-to-Mar correction is not generalized. The late-Ravina, relative-age and Savoraic conclusions, including the Rafram kallah report, remain Hyman’s chronological argument rather than new genealogy or authority admission.
